source.title: Learning ReLU Networks on Linearly Separable Data: Algorithm, Optimality, and Generalization
source.authors: G. Wang; G. Giannakis; Jie Chen

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. No apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training-error outcomes for two-layer ReLU networks under noise-injected SGD and plain SGD, using separable binary datasets rather than the benchmark CNN settings in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper reports empirical success rates for its own noise-injected SGD and plain-vanilla SGD. It does not test CIFAR, corrupted or random labels, convolutional networks, or Adam.
record.test_reason: The study reports optimization results for two-layer, fixed-output-weight ReLU classifiers with hinge loss on linearly separable binary data. These do not test V1's convolutional networks on CIFAR or V2's teacher-student problem and extra-neuron comparison. It does not test depth, signal-preserving initialization, stability thresholds, or batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the authors prove convergence to zero hinge loss in finitely many nonzero updates for their selectively noise-injected SGD on linearly separable data, with fixed second-layer weights containing both signs. They report 100% empirical success, derive generalization bounds, and leave multilayer networks and alternative losses to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The proposed method perturbs selected ReLU activity indicators during SGD; the paper also compares it with plain-vanilla SGD. It uses fixed second-layer weights, hinge loss, and linearly separable binary data.
record.method_sensitivity: Plain-vanilla SGD is more prone to bad local minima at small k in the synthetic Gaussian sweep; the text says learning becomes easier as k grows. Dataset and tested algorithm also differ across the synthetic, iris, and MNIST experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Algorithm 1 attained training hinge loss at most 10^-10 in 100% of trials across the tested synthetic, iris, and binary MNIST settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selective noise injection into ReLU activity indicators enables reliable optimization of fixed-output-weight, two-layer ReLU classifiers on linearly separable binary data.

fits_no_version.finding: Plain SGD sometimes stalls at bad local minima; the Gaussian-data experiment explicitly reports easier optimization with greater hidden width. Uniform, iris, and MNIST success rates are plotted but not numerically recoverable here.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing hidden width can improve plain-SGD optimization success for shallow ReLU classifiers with fixed output weights and hinge loss on separable data.

record.problems: The empirical settings are restricted to single-hidden-layer networks with fixed second-layer weights and linearly separable binary classification. Most per-setting success rates are shown only in figures; experiment variability is not quantified.

untested.parts: All: training classification error of sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including random or corrupted labels, and the specified smaller-model and training-recipe qualifications.
All: teacher-student ReLU problems, joint teacher/student growth, and adding one or two student neurons relative to teacher width.
All: depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training deep plain or residual networks.
All: activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, and initialization comparisons affecting training speed or depth.
All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature evolution, and edge-of-stability training.
All: batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training speed or stability.

record.verdict_notes: The proposed-method rows are valid descriptions of its empirical performance, but should not serve as evidence for V1. V2's teacher-student and relative-width requirements cannot be replaced by a generic width sweep. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; this does not dispute the explicitly reported optimizer successes. The text calls gamma a noise variance in the experiments, whereas the algorithm defines variance as gamma squared, so that parameter notation is ambiguous.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, convolutional networks, Adam, early stopping, and regularized recipes are not tested.
